newsitem.title: INDIA: India ITC shares up 3.9 pct after results.
newsitem.headline: India ITC shares up 3.9 pct after results.

text.p: Shares of India's largest tobacco firm ITC Ltd jumped 10.75 rupees or 3.9 percent to 286.50 in early trade on the Bombay bourse after the firm's first half net beat expectations, traders said.
They said ITC shares climbed 12.25 rupees or 4.4 percent to 289.75 on the National Stock Exchange.
ITC said on Monday net profit rose to 1.81 billion rupees in the first half of 1996/97 (April-March) from 1.41 billion a year ago. Forecasts ranged from 1.5 billion to 1.7 billion rupees.

The firm said its board appointed Ram S. Tarneja and B. Vijayaraghavan as independent, non-executive directors of the company. Britain's B.A.T. Industries Plc is the largest single shareholder of ITC with a 31.7 percent stake.
"The move to hire non-executive directors suggests that B.A.T. is likely to be more active in the firm's management," said a trader at a foreign brokerage.
"There's been strong margin expansion, operating profits are up and volume growth is good suggesting an expansion of market share. The firm has shown all round good results," he said.
